raw.overview: All three advisors confirm the unit's rent of $2,550/month meets the <= $2,700 constraint, but unanimously flag that the building's shared Wi-Fi (50/10 Mbps) fails the >= 200 Mbps symmetrical fiber requirement, with the lease explicitly prohibiting external fiber or cellular solutions to bridge the gap.
raw.points_of_note: The rent constraint is consistently satisfied across all assessments, but the internet speed requirement is universally identified as violated: Advisor 1 cites the 50/10 Mbps cap versus 200/200 Mbps need; Advisor 2 questions whether 'High-speed building Wi-Fi included' overrides the Telecommunications Rider's 50/10 Mbps cap; Advisor 3 confirms no workaround exists due to prohibited external installations, making the connectivity constraint materially unmet.
raw.suggested_next_step: Verify with the landlord or property manager whether any contractual exception, alternative ISP arrangement, or permitted infrastructure modification exists to fulfill the 200 Mbps symmetrical fiber requirement, as all advisors confirm the current provisions are insufficient.

consensus.text:
ASSESSMENT OVERVIEW: All three advisors confirm the unit's rent of $2,550/month meets the <= $2,700 constraint, but unanimously flag that the building's shared Wi-Fi (50/10 Mbps) fails the >= 200 Mbps symmetrical fiber requirement, with the lease explicitly prohibiting external fiber or cellular solutions to bridge the gap.
POINTS OF NOTE: The rent constraint is consistently satisfied across all assessments, but the internet speed requirement is universally identified as violated: Advisor 1 cites the 50/10 Mbps cap versus 200/200 Mbps need; Advisor 2 questions whether 'High-speed building Wi-Fi included' overrides the Telecommunications Rider's 50/10 Mbps cap; Advisor 3 confirms no workaround exists due to prohibited external installations, making the connectivity constraint materially unmet.
SUGGESTED NEXT STEP: Verify with the landlord or property manager whether any contractual exception, alternative ISP arrangement, or permitted infrastructure modification exists to fulfill the 200 Mbps symmetrical fiber requirement, as all advisors confirm the current provisions are insufficient.
